semantic_changes: ca_config_probe now emits phantom_id and second_phantom_id so the admission event and the result event share an identity.
A blocked configuration change is followed by a second RemoveServer for the phantom holder, emitted as ca_config_probe2 with the enqueue outcome and a two-second commit window.

scope.description: The same two-case configuration-change probe on the validated five-voter phantom history, with the probe events now carrying the phantom identity and, when a removal is blocked, a follow-up removal attempt. Case one removes a phantom voter; case two removes a consistent follower; in case two a further RemoveServer for the phantom holder is then attempted with a one-second enqueue timeout and awaited for two seconds.
assumptions: Fault model unchanged: no message loss inside the injected transport; induced events are one partition of two voters from three, retention of the minority suffix, one explicit snapshot, and the RemoveServer attempts.

Both cases keep history, snapshot index, timing and leader load identical so the removed voter's role is the only difference; the follow-up attempt uses the ordinary public API with the documented enqueue timeout.
Reused facilities: MakeClusterCustom with inmemConfig timings, InmemStore, FileSnapshotStore, InmemTransport and MockFSM.
excluded: No production logic was modified; the harness only adds test code.
Automatic snapshotting stays disabled so the published snapshot index is controlled by the explicit Snapshot() call.

basis.prefix: Each case repeats the phantom setup (elect, commit forty entries, partition the leader with one follower, drive forty uncommitted applies on the deposed leader, wait for the pair to stop leading, wait for a majority leader, commit twenty entries and force Snapshot(), heal, wait for both minority members to install the snapshot), records the premise, then issues RemoveServer for the phantom holder or for a consistent follower and waits up to five seconds. When the first removal does not commit, a second RemoveServer for the phantom holder is issued with a one-second enqueue timeout and awaited for two seconds, and both outcomes are emitted.
basis.requirement: A configuration change must either commit or fail observably within a bounded time rather than block indefinitely because a voter whose cached log claim was superseded by its own snapshot can no longer accept log entries, and a blocked change must not prevent the operator from issuing further configuration changes.

comparisons.description: Removing a phantom voter commits promptly: the remaining configuration still contains three voters that accept entries.
Removing a consistent voter does not commit within the window: the new configuration's quorum includes a phantom holder, so the entry cannot gather its acknowledgements.
After the blocked change the operator's follow-up removal of the phantom holder is refused at enqueue time, so the wedge is not limited to the blocked entry itself.
The follow-up change also does not commit within its window, matching the closed configuration-change gate.

before.description: Two cases built on the already validated five-voter phantom history: forty entries committed on all voters, the current leader and one follower partitioned together and given forty further entries that never reach a quorum of five, the remaining three voters electing a leader, committing twenty entries and publishing a snapshot at an index below the suffix end so both minority members become phantom holders after healing. One case then removes a phantom voter; the other removes a consistent follower. Both removals are issued on the majority leader and awaited for five seconds, and the phantom premise is recorded before the attempt.
assumptions: Fault model unchanged: no message loss inside the injected transport; the induced events are one partition of two voters from three, retention of the minority suffix, one explicit snapshot, and one RemoveServer attempt.

The comparison between the two cases holds the history, snapshot index, timing and leader load identical; only the identity of the removed voter differs, and it is chosen so the new configuration's quorum either excludes or includes a phantom holder.
Reused facilities: MakeClusterCustom with inmemConfig timings, InmemStore, FileSnapshotStore, InmemTransport and MockFSM.
excluded: No production logic was modified; the harness only adds test code.
Automatic snapshotting is disabled so the published snapshot index is controlled by the explicit Snapshot() call.

prefix.before: Each case repeats the phantom setup: elect a leader in a five-voter cluster, commit forty entries, partition the leader with one follower, drive forty further applies on the deposed leader so the pair shares an uncommitted suffix, wait for the pair to stop leading, wait for one of the remaining three to be the only stable leader, commit twenty entries there and force Snapshot(), heal the partition and wait until both minority members have installed the snapshot. The case then records the premise (claim above snapshot on both minority members, consistent claim on a majority voter) and issues RemoveServer on the majority leader for either a phantom holder or a consistent follower, waiting up to five seconds for the future and recording whether it committed, the elapsed time, the configuration sizes the leader reports before and after, and whether the removed voter held a phantom claim.
